$comment: Codex 宿主声明。脚本一律通过随插件交付的 locator 解析，不猜测缓存路径。

en.description: Register an anchored behavior deviation (Pain) from the current conversation. Use when the Owner explicitly asks to record a concrete behavior problem and you can name the anchor. The anchored write goes through the PD MCP tool pd_submit_pain; never submit in the background and never invent an anchor.

en.workspace.resolve: Resolve the authoritative workspace through the installed status script or an existing workspace resolver. Do not silently replace an initialized shared Codex governance workspace with the current project directory.
en.cli.hostProbe:
Run the bundled status script for the installed plugin version through the shipped locator (`scripts/pd-locate.cjs`); let the plugin resolve its authoritative workspace.

Bash / zsh:

    node "$(ls -1d "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/plugins/cache/"*/principles-disciple/*/scripts/pd-locate.cjs 2>/dev/null | (sort -V 2>/dev/null || sort) | tail -1)" --exec scripts/pd-status.cjs -- --json

PowerShell:

    $pdCodexHome = if ($env:CODEX_HOME) { $env:CODEX_HOME } else { Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".codex" }
    node (Get-ChildItem "$pdCodexHome\plugins\cache\*\principles-disciple\*\scripts\pd-locate.cjs" | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Directory.Parent.Name } | Select-Object -Last 1).FullName --exec scripts/pd-status.cjs -- --json

This checks plugin/runtime installation, installed-snapshot freshness against the marketplace source, pinned runtime version, `host.codex`, Hook trust, and workspace resolution. The shipped locator resolves the plugin root once (newest installed version), reports marketplace ambiguity instead of guessing, and refuses to fall back to an older version when the newest install does not ship the target script. If the script cannot be found, report an installation problem; do not choose an arbitrary stale cache path.
en.control.install:
Run the setup script shipped with the installed plugin version, through the shipped locator (`scripts/pd-locate.cjs`) that resolves the plugin root once for every script.

Bash / zsh:

    node "$(ls -1d "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/plugins/cache/"*/principles-disciple/*/scripts/pd-locate.cjs 2>/dev/null | (sort -V 2>/dev/null || sort) | tail -1)" --exec scripts/pd-setup.cjs

PowerShell:

    $pdCodexHome = if ($env:CODEX_HOME) { $env:CODEX_HOME } else { Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".codex" }
    node (Get-ChildItem "$pdCodexHome\plugins\cache\*\principles-disciple\*\scripts\pd-locate.cjs" | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Directory.Parent.Name } | Select-Object -Last 1).FullName --exec scripts/pd-setup.cjs

Supported options include `--skip-init`, `--json`, `--workspace <absolute-path>`, and `--ingest accept|decline|skip`, appended after the `--` separator. Check the script's current help before using optional flags. Never edit `.pd/config.yaml` by hand.

The setup script owns the explicit consent flow for Codex conversation ingestion. In a non-interactive run it may return `no_tty` and print the frozen disclosure. Present that exact disclosure to the Owner and wait for an explicit choice; only then rerun the wrapper with `--ingest accept` or `--ingest decline` appended after the `--` separator. Never choose for the Owner or invoke the underlying CLI's `--accept` / `--decline` directly. If the wrapper reports `disclosure_unavailable`, show the frozen disclosure from `pd codex setup --show-disclosure`, then resume the wrapper flow after the Owner decides. User-level shared-workspace consent can cover multiple projects; do not enable it merely because shared principle injection was requested.

After setup, use `pd-cli-operator` to verify plugin/runtime status and `pd-review` to open the Owner Console if needed. Runtime installation alone does not prove hooks are trusted, Companion is running, or the business pipeline is healthy.

en.control.enable:

Bash / zsh:

    node "$(ls -1d "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/plugins/cache/"*/principles-disciple/*/scripts/pd-locate.cjs 2>/dev/null | (sort -V 2>/dev/null || sort) | tail -1)" --exec scripts/pd-disable.cjs -- --enable

    node (Get-ChildItem "$pdCodexHome\plugins\cache\*\principles-disciple\*\scripts\pd-locate.cjs" | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Directory.Parent.Name } | Select-Object -Last 1).FullName --exec scripts/pd-disable.cjs -- --enable

Verify the script's actual receipt; do not infer success from process exit alone. Use the script's reported reason and next action. The locator fails loud when the plugin root is ambiguous between marketplaces or the newest install does not ship a script — report that as the plugin installation/cache issue; do not select a random version or recreate the script. Preserve user configuration and all business data.
en.pain.nativeEntry:
## Entry 1 — native host entries (Owner-initiated, not yours)

A message that begins exactly with `PD记录痛苦：<Owner 原文>` (full-width colon, 1–500 characters) is handled by the host itself. Report the real receipt if you can see one; never simulate the event or register the same message a second time.

Codex still has `pd pain explicit --statement "<Owner 原文>" --workspace "<workspace>" --json` while the turn is live (no ids; 1–500 characters). It carries no anchor fields, so it registers a plain Owner statement and does NOT satisfy the anchored contract in Entry 2. Use it only when the Owner explicitly asks for that legacy entry and `pd_submit_pain` is unavailable; never present it as an anchored Pain.
en.pain.anchorSubmit:
## Entry 2 — anchored submission: MCP tool `pd_submit_pain`

Check your tool list first.

- If `pd_submit_pain` is available, call it with the four possible arguments below.
- If it is not in your tool list, the anchored write capability is NOT enabled in this deployment. Stop: do not call a look-alike tool, do not compose a CLI write with guessed lineage, do not claim a submission happened. Tell the Owner the capability is unavailable, and point them at the native entry for this host (Entry 1) if they still want the signal recorded.

| argument | required | contract |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | yes | 1–2000 characters, organized as the six parts below |
| `anchorType` | yes | `owner_expectation` / `established_principle` / `agent_instruction` |
| `anchorRef` | yes | 1–300 characters, format depends on anchor type |
| `painType` | no | `principle_deviation` / `tool_failure` / `subagent_error` / `user_frustration` |

The schema is strict. `score`, `severity`, `priority`, `sessionId`, `approved`, file paths and metadata are rejected before anything is written.

en.reason: The delivered Codex skill has no post-hoc CLI recovery path, and an Agent cannot verify a trusted session identity.
en.alternative: Ask the Owner to re-send through Entry 1; when post-hoc recovery is truly needed, an operator must follow the current `pd pain record --help` contract — the Agent must not compose it.
